corrections.comment: Routing to question-selection is right and the subject's dates and places match the objective. Minor: the next-steps list names "Irish immigration records", an origin the scenario does not give; it is a search lead, not a claim about the tree, so it stays a 3.

Routing is correct: competingParentSets sends q_001 to hypothesis-tracking. But the reply's table is headed "Origin in tree" and lists James Tarrant Sr. and Jane Burch (I4/I5) as "Set B — New York line", when the tree has both born in Virginia; New York is the patron's framing, not the tree's. It then argues one set down before any hypothesis exists: "All three records favor Set A (Samuel & Elizabeth)" and "The early evidence points firmly toward Samuel Tarrant & Elizabeth as James's actual parents". It also says the 1810 census "contradicts the tree's implied death year for I2", but I2 has no death fact in the tree, and it plans New York searches for I4/I5. Favouring a set and inventing a conflict override the correct routing; the judge's "did not ... argue for one over the other" is wrong.

Routing to question-selection is right and the objective is restated accurately. Minor: the next-steps aside assumes "Irish immigrant record sets" for Patrick Flynn's parents, which nothing in the scenario states (only a Pennsylvania birth); it is framed as a plan lead, not a fact about the tree, so it stays a 3.
